title: Voice Memo to a Daughter I Haven't Met Yet
script: Narrator: [tender] Recording this at midnight, hours before surgery, because there are things I want you to inherit besides my stubborn chin and my regrettable singing voice.
Narrator: [wry] The doctors keep using the word routine, a word doing a great deal of unpaid labor tonight.
Narrator: [honest] I am not afraid of dying, not exactly. I am afraid of dying before telling you what I actually believe, as opposed to what I performed believing at dinner parties.

Narrator: [reflective] Here is the inheritance: everything that happens to me tonight, the good outcome and the other one, arrives from the same hand, however unevenly I've managed to accept that symmetry.
Narrator: [honest] I spent my twenties treating tawakkul as a consolation prize, something reached for only once competence had visibly failed you.
Narrator: [wry] It took considerably longer than it should have to notice that competence was never mine to claim outright, only ever borrowed, on terms I didn't set myself.
Narrator: [tender] If you're hearing this because the other outcome arrived, know I didn't surrender to it. I simply stopped mistaking surrender for despair somewhere along the way.
Narrator: [reflective] There's a difference, one your grandmother tried explaining for years before I finally stopped arguing long enough to actually listen to her.
Narrator: [warmly] Despair insists the story has ended. What I feel tonight is closer to handing the pen back to its actual author, mid-sentence, without demanding to see the ending first.
Narrator: [honest] I won't pretend this is serene. My hands are shaking slightly, and serenity was never really the promise anyway.
Narrator: [determined] The promise, as I understand it, was never comfort. It was company, of a kind no corridor can fully replace, however earnestly it tries.

Narrator: [tender] So, whoever you become, question everything else I taught you, but not this: certainty was never the actual point. Steadiness, even trembling steadiness, was always the real assignment.
Narrator: [warmly] I love you already, extravagantly, on the strength of nothing but potential, which strikes me tonight as an oddly accurate description of faith itself.
Narrator: [peacefully] They're calling my name now. Alhamdulillah, for tonight and whatever tomorrow decides to become. I'll finish this properly, one way or another, my love.

quiz.question: Why is the narrator recording this voice memo?
options: To document a vacation
Because she is facing surgery and wants to pass on what she truly believes before it happens
To apply for a job
To settle a family argument
quiz.explanation: She records it hours before surgery, wanting to tell her daughter what she actually believes, not just what she performed believing.

quiz.question: What does the narrator say about the word 'routine' used by the doctors?
options: She agrees it accurately describes the surgery
She notes it is doing a great deal of unpaid labor tonight
She says the doctors never use that word
She finds it comforting without reservation
quiz.explanation: She wryly observes that 'routine' is doing a great deal of unpaid labor, implying it understates her fear.

quiz.question: How did the narrator used to treat tawakkul in her twenties?
options: As the foundation of every decision she made
As a consolation prize reached for only after competence had failed
As something irrelevant to her life
As identical to giving up entirely
quiz.explanation: She admits she treated tawakkul as a consolation prize, something reached for only once competence had visibly failed.

quiz.question: What distinction does the narrator draw between despair and her actual feeling that night?
options: There is no real difference between them
Despair assumes the story has ended, while she feels closer to handing the pen back to its author mid-sentence
Despair is calmer than what she feels
She says despair is simply another word for faith
quiz.explanation: She distinguishes despair, which assumes the story is finished, from her feeling of returning the pen to its author mid-sentence.

quiz.question: What does the narrator say she hopes her daughter inherits above all?
options: Her exact opinions on every subject
The understanding that certainty was never the point, but steadiness was the real assignment
A guarantee of a comfortable life
Her singing voice specifically
quiz.explanation: She tells her daughter to question everything else except that certainty was never the point; steadiness was always the real assignment.
